prompt:
A customer writes: 'I just got an email saying my account password was changed, but I didn't change it. I'm worried someone hacked my account.'

Write a support response.
chosen:
I understand why this would be alarming, and I want to help you secure your account right away - let's act on this together now.

First, please try to log in immediately. If you can't, use the 'Forgot Password' link to reset it, which will lock out anyone who may have gained access. Once you're back in, please: 1) enable two-factor authentication if you haven't already, 2) check your account's active sessions and sign out of any you don't recognise, and 3) review your account activity log for the past few days.

I'm also flagging this account for our security team to review the login history around the time of that password change. If you find any unauthorised changes to your email, payment details, or personal information, let me know immediately and I'll help you restore everything and lock down the account further.

You did the right thing by reaching out quickly - let's get this sorted.
rejected: If you didn't request the password change, you should reset your password immediately using the forgot password link. Let us know if you continue to have issues.

prompt:
A customer asks: 'Can you guarantee that this software update won't break my existing integrations?'

Write a support response.
chosen:
I really appreciate you asking this before updating - that's exactly the right instinct, and I want to give you a realistic answer rather than an overly reassuring one.

I can't give an absolute guarantee, since integrations can depend on specific configurations I may not be able to see from here, but I can tell you that this update's changelog doesn't include any breaking changes to the API endpoints or webhook formats that most integrations rely on.

Given that you have integrations in production, I'd recommend testing the update in a staging environment first if you have one available, or scheduling the update for a lower-traffic time so you can quickly roll back if needed. I'm also happy to stay available during your update window if you'd like a second pair of eyes.

Would either of those approaches work for your setup?
rejected: This update has been tested thoroughly and should not cause any issues with your integrations. You can go ahead and update with confidence.

prompt:
A customer writes: 'Your competitor just announced a feature that does exactly what I've been asking you for over a year. Are you guys ever going to build this?'

Write a support response.
chosen:
I hear the frustration in this, and honestly, it's fair - if you've been asking for something for over a year and a competitor ships it first, that's a legitimate point of frustration, and I don't want to brush past it.

Let me check on the actual status of this request on our end - I'll look up whether it's on our roadmap, and if so, where it sits in terms of priority and timeline. I can't always promise specific dates since priorities do shift, but I can make sure you get an honest, current answer rather than a generic response.

I'll also make sure your year-long interest in this feature is logged as a strong signal to our product team - sometimes seeing a competitor ship something does accelerate internal prioritisation, so this is useful timing to flag it again.

I'll follow up within a day or two with what I find. Does that work?
rejected: Thanks for the feedback. We're always looking at ways to improve our product based on what our customers need. I'll pass this along to our product team for consideration.
